title: Iridescent oil slick from thin-film interference
purpose: Generate tileable maps of thin-film interference colours: oil on puddles in asphalt, a spill on harbour water, a soap film or heat tint on steel, with colours computed from film thickness, refractive indices and colour-matching functions. Use for wet streets, polluted water, bubbles and welded metal.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python oil_slick_iridescent.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.meaning: Thickness layout: 0 swirls of warped noise, 1 bands thinning away from weld lines.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.meaning: Swirls or bands across the tile.

parameters.name: swirl
parameters.meaning: Domain warping of the film into marbled swirls.

parameters.name: coverage
parameters.meaning: Share of the surface under liquid (asphalt and water bases); 1 covers it all.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Oil on puddles in dark asphalt: rainbow swirls on flat water, dry rough stone around.

presets.name: harbour_water
presets.description: A spill on dark harbour water covering the whole surface in broad swirls.

presets.name: soap_film
presets.description: Soap film in air: vivid swirling bands that go black where the film is thinnest.

presets.name: tempered_steel
presets.description: Heat tint on steel: straw, bronze, purple and blue bands beside weld lines.

limits: Two-beam interference at normal incidence: colours do not shift with viewing angle, multiple reflections and absorption are ignored, and a metal substrate is approximated by a negative real reflection amplitude instead of a complex index, so temper colours are close but not exact. The colour-matching functions are an analytic Gaussian fit and the grey part of the film reflectance is partly removed for clearer hues, so this is a stylized rendering of thin-film colour rather than a spectral measurement. Film thickness comes from noise or bands, not from flow or oxidation physics. One still frame.
